issues.description: Test fix.text values contradict the fixed code in new reject cases
issues.detail: New reject fixtures for `oklch(from red l c 10)` and `hsl(from red 10 s l)` declare fix.text as `'0deg'` while the fixed output is clearly `10deg`/`120deg`. Either the fixtures are passing by accident or the payloads are wrong. A future maintainer cannot tell which behavior is intended. Make fixtures match reality.

issues.description: Relative-color detection and channel indexing are complected via undocumented `+ offset` arithmetic
issues.detail: findHue braids three concerns: detecting `from`, computing a channel offset, and indexing args. The invariant that args[1] is the base color and channels begin at index 2 is never stated. A small helper returning the channel sub-list (or a named hueIndex) would name the concern once instead of smearing it across two `+ offset` sites, preventing off-by-one when grammar evolves.

issues.description: `args[0 + offset]` is cosmetic noise; use a named index or drop the `0 +`
issues.detail: Writing `args[0 + offset]` reads as comment-in-arithmetic rather than a named channel index. Either fold the literal indices 0 and 2 into named constants applied to a channels array, or compute the absolute index once. Pure readability cleanup with no behavior change.

issues.description: Missing nested-relative-color test where outer hue should still be flagged
issues.detail: Coverage includes a nested-good path and a mixed nested+outer case, but not a reject where only the outer function's hue position is bad (or a chained `oklch(from oklch(from red l c h) l c h)`). Adding one pins down that findHue handles nested relative chains correctly and guards against future regressions.

synthesis.summary: Panel verdict: NEEDS-WORK but close to ship. The patch correctly fixes a real bug with a minimal offset shift and the test matrix covers accept/reject, case-insensitive `FROM`, and a nested function case. Two concerns block a clean land: the new reject fixtures' `fix.text` payloads say `'0deg'` while the fixed output is `10deg`/`120deg`, which is either wrong or passing by accident; and the `+ offset` arithmetic complects relative-color detection with channel indexing without naming the invariant. Cosmetic cleanup of `args[0 + offset]` and one additional nested-relative-color test would close the remaining gaps.
